chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Musa ibn Ja'far from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Sadqa who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: 'Some of our companions have narrated that it is permissible for a man to marry the slave-girl of his son or the slave-girl of his daughter. I have a daughter, and for my daughter there is a slave-girl that I bought for her as part of her dowry. Is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her?' He said: 'No, except with her permission.'

Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: 'Is it not established that this is permissible?' He said: 'Yes, that is if he is the one who caused it (bought it).' Then he turned to me and pointed with his index finger and said: 'If you buy a slave-girl for your daughter or for your son, and the son is young and has not had intercourse with her, it is permissible for you to take possession of her and marry her. Otherwise, no, except with the permission of both (the son and the slave-girl). This does not contradict the earlier reports, because his saying 'It is permissible for you to take possession of her and marry her' is understood to mean that it is permissible for you if you have valued her and the price has become due in your debt for your child. As for before that, it is not permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father marry the slave-girl owned by his minor son?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of 'qist' (valuation) regarding a father's right to marry the slave-girl owned by his minor son. He distinguishes between the father purchasing the girl specifically for the son (where the father may marry her after assuming the debt) versus general ownership, thereby reconciling apparent contradictions in earlier hadiths by emphasizing the condition of the son's age and consummation. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that paternal authority over a minor's property is contingent upon the child's capacity to consent or consummate the marriage.
